'''''Argyroderma testiculare''''' (Afrikaans: ''bokklootjies'') is a species of [[Succulent plant|succulents]] endemic to the quartz gravel of the [[Knersvlakte]] region. of [[South Africa]]'s [[Western Cape]]. It belongs to the ''[[Aizoaceae]]'' family, and is listed as rare on the [[South African National Biodiversity Institute|SANBI]] Red List, because it occurs in an area smaller than 68 km<sup>2</sup>, but it is not endangered there.<ref name="SANBI"/>
[[File:Argyroderma_testiculare_-_RSA5.jpg|left|thumb|Argyroderma testiculare]]
It is a small plant that does not grow larger than 15 cm. The leaves are thick and look like an egg which has been chopped in half. The flowers are purple with a yellow centre.<ref>{{Cite web|title=houseplantexpert|url=http://www.houseplantsexpert.com/argyroderma-testiculare.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171129025102/https://www.houseplantsexpert.com/argyroderma-testiculare.html|archive-date=29 November 2017|language=en}}</ref>

== Conservation status ==
''Argyroderma testiculare'' has an [[Extent of occurrence|EOO]] of 68 km<sup>2</sup>, thus giving it the classification of ''Rare.'' There are no severe threats to the species as most of its habitat is protected.<ref name="SANBI" />
